req.title: Retrieve all players
req.statement: The system shall respond to GET /players with a JSON array of all players in the database.

doc.reasoning: The requirement mandates GET /players/ returns HTTP 200 with a JSON array of all Player objects. I design: (1) a positive EP test verifying exact status code, content-type, array length (26 rows), and spot-checking known player fields; (2) a negative NEG test verifying that an unsupported HTTP method (POST without body / wrong method) returns a non-200 status, and that a malformed path returns 404 not 200; (3) a BVA boundary test verifying the exact count of 26 players (boundary: neither 0 nor 27), checking first and last squad numbers present, and verifying the cache header is either HIT or MISS with exact string values. Additional tests cover: response body is a list not a dict, each item contains the required 'id' field as a UUID string, and the X-Cache header mutation resilience.

tests.name: test_get_all_players_returns_200_with_json_array
preconditions: Database is pre-loaded with exactly 26 player rows
FastAPI app is running in-process via TestClient
actions: Inspect status code, Content-Type header, and response body
expected: Response body is a JSON array of exactly 26 Player objects
Each object contains keys: id, firstName, lastName, squadNumber, position
trace: R-PLAYER-001: GET /players/ -> HTTP 200; JSON array of Player objects
tests.executable:
from main import app
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient

def test_get_all_players_returns_200_with_json_array():
    client = TestClient(app)
    response = client.get('/players/')
    assert response.status_code == 200
    assert 'application/json' in response.headers['content-type']
    body = response.json()
    assert isinstance(body, list)
    assert len(body) == 26
    required_keys = {'id', 'firstName', 'lastName', 'squadNumber', 'position'}
    for player in body:
        assert required_keys.issubset(player.keys()), f'Missing keys in {player}'

test_get_all_players_returns_200_with_json_array()

from main import app
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient

def test_get_all_players_exact_known_player_fields():
    client = TestClient(app)
    response = client.get('/players/')
    assert response.status_code == 200
    body = response.json()
    messi = next((p for p in body if p['squadNumber'] == 10), None)
    assert messi is not None
    assert messi['firstName'] == 'Lionel'
    assert messi['middleName'] == 'Andrés'
    assert messi['lastName'] == 'Messi'
    assert messi['position'] == 'Right Winger'
    assert messi['abbrPosition'] == 'RW'
    assert messi['team'] == 'Paris Saint-Germain'
    assert messi['league'] == 'Ligue 1'
    assert messi['starting11'] == True
    assert messi['id'] == 'acc433bf-d505-51fe-831e-45eb44c4d43c'

tests.name: test_get_all_players_cache_header_present_and_valid
preconditions: Database is pre-loaded with 26 player rows
Cache may be cold (MISS) or warm (HIT) depending on prior requests
actions: First call: assert X-Cache is either MISS or HIT (exact strings)
Second call: assert X-Cache is HIT (cache warmed by first call)
expected: First call X-Cache header is 'MISS' or 'HIT'
Second call X-Cache header is exactly 'HIT'
trace: R-PLAYER-001: caching behaviour; STC cold->warm state transition on X-Cache header
tests.executable:
from main import app
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient

def test_get_all_players_cache_header_present_and_valid():
    client = TestClient(app)
    r1 = client.get('/players/')
    assert r1.status_code == 200
    assert r1.headers.get('x-cache') in ('HIT', 'MISS')
    r2 = client.get('/players/')
    assert r2.status_code == 200
    assert r2.headers.get('x-cache') == 'HIT'
    assert r2.headers.get('x-cache') != 'MISS'

test_get_all_players_cache_header_present_and_valid()

tests.name: test_get_all_players_each_item_has_valid_uuid_id
preconditions: Database is pre-loaded with 26 player rows each having a UUID id
actions: For each player in the response, parse the 'id' field as a UUID
expected: Every player object has an 'id' field parseable as a valid UUID
trace: R-PLAYER-001: JSON array of Player objects; each Player must have a valid UUID id
tests.executable:
from main import app
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient
from uuid import UUID

def test_get_all_players_each_item_has_valid_uuid_id():
    client = TestClient(app)
    response = client.get('/players/')
    assert response.status_code == 200
    body = response.json()
    assert len(body) == 26
    for player in body:
        assert 'id' in player
        parsed = UUID(player['id'])
        assert str(parsed) == player['id']
    messi = next(p for p in body if p['squadNumber'] == 10)
    assert messi['id'] == 'acc433bf-d505-51fe-831e-45eb44c4d43c'

test_get_all_players_each_item_has_valid_uuid_id()
